newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt to push new theme-store concept.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt to push new theme-store concept.

text.p: German department store group Karstadt AG said on Wednesday that sales were going well at its refurbished outlet in the city of Duisburg, and it would upgrade other branches on a new theme-based approach.

Chief executive Walter Deuss told the company's annual shareholders' meeting that sales were up by around 10 percent at the Duisburg outlet, which was remodelled in April to focus on fashion products.
At the same time, Deuss said, the range of goods on offer at the store had been cut by 40 percent.
"The reaction of our customers has been extremely positive. The average amount that they spend is also much higher than the company average," he added.
Deuss said refurbishment work had begun at Karstadt's Duesseldorf branch and should be completed in October, while another store had already been upgraded in Rosenheim.
Retail analysts have been following Karstadt's Duisburg pilot project with interest to see whether applying the new lifestyle theme approach would help turn around the group's weak earnings.

Karstadt has been badly hit by four years of falling demand in the retail sector and the costly takeover and integration of the loss-making Hertie department store chain. The company has proposed cutting the 1996 dividend to 10 marks from 13 marks.
Deuss also said that, based on five-month group figures, the Karstadt group was on course to post a net profit of around 150 million marks, up from 58.6 million in 1996.
